title: 真假金丝雀的博弈第16章
content_zh:
第16章 她的选择

    周六上午，我约了顾明珠。

    地点没有选在顾西辞的办公室。上次在那里见面是为了给她施压，让她在顾西辞的地盘上说实话。这次不一样，这次是谈，不是审。我把地点定在思南路那家“隐溪”茶馆，就是上次林曼如约我的地方。二楼的包间，竹影映在窗帘上，茶壶坐在小炉子上咕噜咕噜地响。

    顾明珠比约定时间早了十分钟到。她今天没穿那件松松垮垮的灰色卫衣，换了一件白色衬衫，领口熨得很平，头发扎成了低马尾。眼眶下面还是有一点黑眼圈，但比上次淡了很多。

    “姐。”她在门口站了一下，叫了我一声。

    “进来坐。”

    她在我对面坐下，把背包放在旁边的椅子上。那只毛绒小熊还挂在拉链上，脏了一点，鼻尖的线头松了。

    “你找我什么事？”

    “先喝茶。”

    我给她倒了一杯正山小种。她端起来抿了一口，放下。两只手交叠放在膝盖上，背挺得很直，像个等待面试的学生。她以前不是这样的，认亲宴上她挽着顾西辞手臂的时候，下巴是扬起来的。现在她的下巴收着，眼睛看着我，但目光不是躲闪的，是在等。

    “最近怎么样？”我问。

    “还行。上课，回家，睡觉。”

    “林薇还在联系你吗？”

    “没有。上次之后她给我发过一条消息，我没回。她又发了一条，我直接拉黑了。”

    “很好。”

    “不好。”她忽然把茶杯往前推了半寸，“拉黑她之后，我手机通讯录里只剩下三个人。顾太太——我妈，但她从来不给我打电话。顾西辞，他也没有给我打过电话。还有你。”

    “同学呢？”

    “同学不知道我是谁。我在学校里没有说过我的身份。顾家把消息压下来了，只有圈内人知道真假千金的事。”她端起茶杯又放下，“所以拉黑了林薇之后，除了你，没有人会主动联系我。”

    她的声音很平静，不像上次那样压着嗓子哭，但每个字都是凉的。不是愤怒的凉，是孤独的凉。我理解这种感觉。三个月前我从顾家出来，手机通讯录里也只剩下三个人——顾西辞、李婶、还有那个把我行李放在后门的管家李叔。

    “那你接下来打算怎么办？”

    “什么怎么办？”

    “你的生活。总不能一直上课回家睡觉。”

    她抬起头看我，眼睛里多了一点警觉。不是对我的警觉，是对这个话题本身的警觉。

    “你想说什么？”

    “我想知道，你有没有想过以后做什么。”

    “我能做什么？顾家把我找回来，不是因为我有什么本事，是因为我身上流着顾家的血。我的作用就是当顾家的女儿，跟顾西辞结婚，生一个姓顾的孩子。其他的不需要我做。”

    “谁跟你说的？”

    “没有人跟我说。但我看得出来。”她把茶杯端起来，这次没有抿一口就放下，而是实实在在地喝了一口，“我妈对我好，但她的好是有分寸的。她给我买衣服，给我安排学校，但她从来不让我进书房。顾家的书房，你以前随便进的吧？”

    “是。”

    “我进不去。有一次我推门进去想找本书看，我爸——顾先生——正在里面打电话。他看到我，第一反应是把桌上的文件翻过来扣住。然后他笑着说‘明珠啊，书房里都是商业文件，你不感兴趣的’。他连问都没问我为什么进来。”

    “所以你觉得顾家不需要你的本事。”

    “不是觉得。是事实。”她放下茶杯，“你呢？你找我到底想说什么？”

    我把茶壶端起来，给我们俩都续了杯。窗外竹影在窗帘上晃动，包间里只有小炉子的咕噜声和她略显急促的呼吸声。

    “我这边有一个工作机会。不是全职，是兼职。你可以一边上学一边做。”

    她的表情变了一下。不是惊喜，是意外加上怀疑。

    “什么工作？”

    “方总——就是顾氏并购案的合作方，他那边在筹备一个新的文娱板块，需要做一些年轻用户群体的消费习惯调研。目标人群是十八到二十四岁的大学生。你刚好在这个年龄段里。”

    “你要我去做问卷？”

    “不是问卷。是深度访谈。你自己去找身边不同类型的大学生聊天，记录他们每个月花多少钱、花在哪里、怎么选品牌、关注什么社交媒体。整理成一份调研报告。”
content_en:
Chapter 16 Her choice

    On Saturday morning, I made an appointment with Gu Mingzhu.

    The location was not chosen in Gu Xici's office. The last time they met there was to put pressure on her to tell the truth on Gu Xici's territory. This time is different. This time it is a discussion, not a trial. I set the location at the "Yinxi" teahouse on Sinan Road, the same place where Lin Man kept my appointment last time. In the private room on the second floor, bamboo shadows were reflected on the curtains, and the teapot sat on the small stove and purred.

    Gu Mingzhu arrived ten minutes earlier than the agreed time. She didn't wear the baggy gray sweatshirt today, but changed into a white shirt. The collar was pressed flat and her hair was tied into a low ponytail. There are still some dark circles under the eyes, but they are much lighter than last time.

    "Sister." She stopped at the door and called me.

    "Come in and sit down."

    She sat down across from me and put her backpack on the chair next to her. The stuffed bear was still hanging on the zipper, a little dirty, and the thread on the tip of its nose was loose.

    "What do you want from me?"

    "Drink tea first."

    I poured her a glass of Lapsang Souchong. She picked it up, took a sip, and put it down. His hands were folded on his knees, and his back was straight, like a student waiting for an interview. She wasn't like this before. When she held Gu Xici's arm at the wedding reception, her chin was raised. Now her chin is tucked and her eyes are looking at me, but her eyes are not evasive, they are waiting.

    "How are you doing?" I asked.

    "It's okay. Go to class, go home, and sleep."

    "Is Lin Wei still contacting you?"

    "No. She sent me a message after the last time, but I didn't reply. She sent another message, and I blocked her directly."

    "Very good."

    "No." She suddenly pushed the tea cup forward half an inch. "After blocking her, there are only three people left in the address book of my mobile phone. Mrs. Gu - my mother, but she never called me. Gu Xici, he never called me either. And you."

    "Where are the classmates?"

    "My classmates don't know who I am. I never told my identity in school. The Gu family suppressed the news. Only insiders know about the real and fake daughter." She picked up the tea cup and put it down again, "So after blocking Lin Wei, no one will contact me except you."

    Her voice was calm, not like she was crying at the top of her voice like last time, but every word was cold. Not an angry Ryo, but a lonely Ryo. I understand this feeling. I left Gu's house three months ago, and there were only three people left in my phone address book - Gu Xici, Aunt Li, and the housekeeper, Uncle Li, who put my luggage at the back door.

    "Then what are you going to do next?"

    "What to do?"

    "Your life. You can't go home and sleep in class all the time."

    She looked up at me, her eyes a little more alert. Not alarm about me, but alarm about the topic itself.

    "What do you want to say?"

    "I want to know if you have ever thought about what you will do in the future."

    "What can I do? The Gu family brought me back, not because I have any abilities, but because I have the blood of the Gu family. My role is to be the daughter of the Gu family, marry Gu Xici, and have a child named Gu. I don't need to do anything else."

    "Who told you?"

    "No one told me. But I can see it." She picked up the tea cup and put it down without taking a sip this time, but took a real sip. "My mother is good to me, but her kindness is measured. She buys me clothes and arranges schools for me, but she never lets me enter the study room. You can enter the Gu family's study room casually before, right?"

    "Yes."

    "I couldn't get in. One time I opened the door and went in looking for a book to read. My dad - Mr. Gu - was on the phone inside. When he saw me, his first reaction was to turn over the documents on the table and clasp them. Then he smiled and said, 'Mingzhu, the study is full of business documents, and you are not interested'. He didn't even ask me why I came in."

    "So you think the Gu family doesn't need your skills."

    "It's not a feeling. It's a fact." She put down the tea cup, "What about you? What do you want to say to me?"

    I picked up the teapot and refilled the cups for both of us. The bamboo shadows outside the window swayed on the curtains, and the only sounds in the private room were the grunting of the small stove and her slightly rapid breathing.

    "I have a job opportunity here. It's not full time, it's part time. You can do it while going to school."

    Her expression changed. It's not a surprise, it's an accident plus suspicion.

    "What job?"

    "Mr. Fang is the partner of Gu's merger and acquisition project. He is preparing a new entertainment sector and needs to do some research on the consumption habits of young user groups. The target group is college students aged 18 to 24. You happen to be in this age group."

    "You want me to take a questionnaire?"

    "It's not a questionnaire. It's an in-depth interview. You go and chat with different types of college students around you, and record how much money they spend every month, where they spend it, how they choose brands, and what social media they follow. Compile it into a research report."
title_en: The Game of True and False Canaries Chapter 16
